title: Friendship
lead: The Bible prizes the friend who stays loyal in hard days and warns against the friend who turns. Proverbs and Ben Sira give practical rules for keeping friends; David and Jonathan show friendship at its deepest; God calls Abraham his friend; Jesus calls his disciples friends and lays down his life for them.

sections.b: Proverbs says, "At every time a friend keeps loving, / and a brother is born for the hard days" (Proverbs 17:17), and warns that a crowd of friends is not the same as one who holds on "tighter than a brother" (Proverbs 18:24). Jonathan loved David "as much as his own life" (1 Samuel 18:1). The betrayal of a friend is one of the Psalms' deepest griefs: "the one I trusted, / who ate my bread, / has raised his heel high against me" (Psalm 41:9), words Jesus applies to Judas (John 13:18). Abraham "was called the friend of God" (James 2:23; compare Isaiah 41:8), and the LORD spoke to Moses "as anyone talks with a close companion" (Exodus 33:11). Jesus gives friendship its fullest meaning: "There is no greater love anyone can have than this: to lay down his life for the sake of his friends" (John 15:13).
